items.detail:
The added paragraph pins the stale-diff half but stops short of the stronger form of the same defect. `loop/run.mjs` runs the gates once, at line 342, before the review loop, and never re-runs them after the revision commit at line 505 — while `runReview` reads `sha` fresh from the branch head (`loop/lib/review.mjs:715`, `const before = rev-parse branch`) and hands it to `gatesSection`. So a pass-2 brief's sentence "The loop ran these itself, in this branch's own worktree, immediately before this review on commit `d29ae884daf0`" states a PASS measured on the PRE-revision tree under the POST-revision SHA. That is the same mismatch as the diff, in the section the brief tells the reviewer not to re-run — one added sentence to the evidence paragraph would record it, and the machinery job's "check that fails loudly if the two disagree" should cover the gate result as well as the diff text.

items.detail:
The revised summary says GLM-5.3 stands "third on the card's own row (behind Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol)" — literally accurate, but the card's ExploitGym footnote reads "We evaluate GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3 and Qwen3.8 Max in Claude Code 2.1.207" and names TPS rescaling factors for exactly those three (115 / 40 / 47). It says nothing about where the Fable 5 (181/247), GPT-5.6 Sol (216/293) or Opus 4.8 (80/120) figures came from, or whether the same rescaled budget applies to them. So the ranking the summary now cedes is a comparison between a number Z.ai measured under a stated method and three numbers whose method the card does not state. Fix: when the post is written, add half a sentence to the evidence block saying the card states its ExploitGym method for GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max only — so the post inherits the asymmetry instead of presenting the row as one like-for-like leaderboard.

items.detail:
The openai-astra-critical-cyber-designation docket anchors on https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/. Fetched twice during this review, that URL returned "The server returned HTTP 403 Forbidden" both times. The page exists and the docket's quotes are corroborated by third parties (SecurityWeek gives "Astra now declines 91.5% of cyber-related jailbreak attempts in its testing, up from 59% for its predecessor, GPT-5.6 Sol"; TechCrunch, 2026-09-01, gives the perfect ExploitBench score and the two zero-days), but a post job told to re-fetch and quote the announcement page directly will be blocked by the same 403. The docket should name a retrieval route that works, or the job should expect to quote the corroborating coverage and say so.
